---
title: "Dashboards"
---

## Overview

A dashboard arranges a document's outputs (plots, tables, numbers, text) into
a grid of cards that fills the browser window. Add `format: dashboard` to the
front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "Sales"
format: dashboard
---
```

Headings lay the page out as rows and columns. Code cells and `.card` divs
become cards. Value boxes, sidebars and toolbars add summary numbers and
controls. The result is a single HTML page built on
[Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com) and the
[bslib](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/) card and sidebar components.

Dashboards in Quarto 2 follow Quarto 1's dashboard format closely, so existing
dashboards should port with few or no changes.
[Differences from Quarto 1](#differences-from-quarto-1) lists where they
differ.

## Layout

### Rows and columns

Each level-2 heading (`##`) starts a row, and each level-3 heading (`###`)
inside it starts a column:

````markdown
---
title: "Layout"
format: dashboard
---

## Row {height=70%}

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

## Row {height=30%}

### Column {width=40%}

```{r}
summary(cars)
```

### Column {width=60%}

```{r}
hist(cars$speed)
```
````

Set `orientation: columns` to swap the roles: level-2 headings become columns
and level-3 headings become rows inside them.

```yaml
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: columns
```

The orientation always follows nesting depth: under `orientation: rows`, a
`##` section is a row and a `###` section inside it is a column, wherever the
headings appear. The heading text itself is not displayed; it only names the
section.

### Sizing: `height`, `width`, fill and flow

Give a row a `height` or a column a `width` as an attribute on its heading.
Percentages share the space between siblings; other CSS units (`300px`,
`20em`) fix the size. Sections without a size share what is left.

By default a dashboard *fills* the window: rows stretch to use the full height
and cards grow with them. A card or section that should keep its natural
height instead *flows*. Add `.flow` to the heading (or `.fill` to force
filling):

```markdown
## Row {.flow}
```

Text-only cards flow automatically, so a row of explanatory text doesn't
stretch to half the page.

### Scrolling

With `scrolling: true` the page grows with its content and scrolls, instead
of fitting the window:

```yaml
format:
  dashboard:
    scrolling: true
```

### Pages

Level-1 headings (`#`) split the dashboard into pages, listed as tabs in the
navigation bar:

```markdown
# Overview

## Row

...

# Details {orientation="columns" scrolling="true"}

## Column

...
```

A page can set its own `orientation` and `scrolling`. The page in the URL hash
(`dashboard.html#details`) opens first, so you can link to a page directly.

## Cards

### Cells and `.card` divs

Every code cell with output becomes a card. A cell's `title` option gives the
card a title:

````markdown
```{r}
#| title: "Stopping distance"
plot(cars)
```
````

Any markdown can go in a card through a `.card` div:

```markdown
::: {.card title="About this dashboard"}
The data come from the 1920s `cars` dataset.
:::
```

Card options, on the cell or the div:

| Option        | Effect                                                          |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `title`       | The card's header text. Inline markdown (code, emphasis) works. |
| `padding`     | Padding around the card body, e.g. `padding: 0`.                |
| `height`      | A fixed height, as for rows.                                    |
| `expandable`  | `false` removes the button that opens the card full screen.     |
| `.fill` / `.flow` | Whether the card stretches or keeps its natural height.     |

Cards are expandable by default. Set `expandable: false` under
`format: dashboard` to turn that off for every card.

### Tabsets

Add `.tabset` to a row or column heading to show its cards as tabs inside one
card. Each card's title becomes its tab label:

````markdown
## Row {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: "Speed"
hist(cars$speed)
```

```{r}
#| title: "Distance"
hist(cars$dist)
```
````

## Value boxes

A value box shows a single number with a title and an optional icon. Write it
as a `.valuebox` div whose first paragraph (or heading) is the title and
second is the value:

```markdown
::: {.valuebox icon="pencil" color="primary"}
Articles per day

45
:::
```

Or produce it from a cell with `content: valuebox`, printing a list (R) or a
dict (Python) with `value` and, optionally, `icon` and `color`:

````markdown
```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Spam"
list(icon = "trash", color = "danger", value = 12)
```
````

The output is read, not evaluated. If it doesn't have the expected shape,
Quarto warns ([`Q-27-1`](/errors/dashboard/Q-27-1.qmd)) and shows the printed
text as the value.

- `icon` is a [Bootstrap Icons](https://icons.getbootstrap.com) name.
- `color` is a Bootstrap theme color (`primary`, `success`, `danger`, …) or any
  CSS color. `bg-color` and `fg-color` set the background and text colors
  separately.
- `showcase-position` (or `showcase`) moves the icon: `left-center` (the
  default), `top-right` or `bottom`.

## Sidebars and toolbars

### Page sidebars

A section whose heading has the `.sidebar` class becomes a collapsible sidebar
next to the rest of its page:

````markdown
## {.sidebar width="250px"}

Filters and notes go here.

## Column

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
````

A sidebar placed after the content goes on the right. A level-1 `.sidebar`
heading before the pages makes a *global* sidebar shared by every page. A
sidebar inside a row applies to that row only.

Headings inside a sidebar are styled as small headings, not as new sections.

### Toolbars

A `.toolbar` section is a horizontal strip above (or, placed after the
content, below) the rest of its page or row. Set its `height` with an
attribute:

```markdown
## {.toolbar}

Choose a region: ...
```

A cell with `content: sidebar` or `content: toolbar` makes a sidebar or
toolbar from its output, without a heading.

### Card toolbars and card sidebars

A `.card-toolbar` div (or a cell with `content: card-toolbar`) adds a toolbar
to a card's header. A `.card-sidebar` div (or `content: card-sidebar`) adds a
sidebar inside the card. By default either attaches to the card that follows
it:

```markdown
::: {.card-toolbar}
Options for the next card.
:::

::: {.card title="Results"}
...
:::
```

To place it somewhere else:

- `target-element="previous"` (toolbars) or `target="previous"` (sidebars)
  attaches it to the card before it. A previous-card toolbar goes in the
  card's footer.
- `header-for="<id>"` or `footer-for="<id>"` puts a toolbar in the header or
  footer of the card with that id, or of the card holding an element with
  that id. `target="<id>"` does the same for a sidebar.
- A card sidebar's `position` is `left` or `right`, and its `width` sets its
  width.

A toolbar or sidebar that finds no card is left out with a warning
([`Q-27-2`](/errors/dashboard/Q-27-2.qmd)).

## Navigation bar

The navigation bar shows the document's `title`, `subtitle` and authors, and
the page tabs. Under `format: dashboard` you can add:

- `logo`: an image path, `{path, alt}`, or `{light, dark}` variants. A logo
  set in `_quarto.yml` is resolved relative to the project, so it works on
  pages in any directory.
- `nav-buttons`: links at the end of the navigation bar. Use `linkedin`,
  `facebook`, `reddit` or `twitter` for share links to the current page, or a
  map with `href` and, optionally, `icon`, `text`, `title`, `rel`, `target`
  and `aria-label`:

```yaml
format:
  dashboard:
    logo: images/logo.png
    nav-buttons:
      - twitter
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto
```

An unknown alias is left out with a warning
([`Q-27-3`](/errors/dashboard/Q-27-3.qmd)).

With a light and a dark theme, the navigation bar gets a dark-mode toggle:

```yaml
format:
  dashboard:
    theme:
      light: flatly
      dark: darkly
```

## Dashboards in websites

A page with `format: dashboard` can be part of a website. It keeps the site's
navigation bar, with the dashboard's own bar (title and page tabs) under it,
and the site footer. It uses the site's `format: html` theme unless the page
sets a theme of its own.

## Previewing

`q2 preview` shows a live preview of a dashboard that updates as you edit,
with working page tabs, card tabs, sidebars and full-screen cards.

## Differences from Quarto 1

Quarto 2 fixes several Quarto 1 dashboard bugs rather than reproducing them:

- Orientation follows nesting depth. Quarto 1 flipped it on every change of
  heading level, so a deeper heading before shallower ones could turn rows
  into columns.
- `.fill` and `.flow` on a row or column heading size the grid, as the
  Quarto 1 documentation describes.
- A toolbar's `height` is honored.
- Headings inside sidebars and toolbars are demoted, as they are in cards.
- `content: sidebar` and `content: toolbar` cells work.
- A value box's title can be a paragraph or a heading, and it always shows.
  Quarto 1 nested paragraphs, which hid the documented form's title.
- `showcase-position` is honored, with `showcase` as an alias.
- `header-for` and `footer-for` accept the card's or cell's own id. Quarto 1
  failed with an error.
- A card toolbar or sidebar that finds no card is a warning with a location,
  not a fatal error or a silent drop.
- A card's `height` is no longer copied onto its body.
- Empty rows and columns are dropped consistently. Quarto 1 kept the last
  empty one.
- A single-page dashboard with a dark theme gets the toggle in its navigation
  bar. Quarto 1 only added it with pages.
- Share links leave out the title when the document has none, instead of
  `title=undefined`.
- In a website, the site's html theme is used only when the dashboard page
  sets no theme. Quarto 1 replaced even the page's own theme.

## Not yet supported

- Shiny (`server: shiny`) and Observable JS dashboards.
- Interactive DataTables / itables tables. Static markdown tables work.
- Arranging several outputs in one card with `layout-ncol`.
- `title`, `padding` and `content` options on **Jupyter** (Python, Julia)
  cells: they are not passed on yet, so such cells become untitled cards and
  `content: valuebox` has no effect. R (knitr) cells, `.card` and `.valuebox`
  divs work.
- The `github` nav-button alias. Give the repository URL as a link instead.
- The dark-mode toggle in the live preview.
